Selected work

Three games, each proving a different range.

All built solo, spanning survival, Souls-like, and MMORPG. The viewport frames below are ready for gameplay captures — swap in a screenshot or clip and each becomes the proof the systems are real.

01 / FLAGSHIP
Survival Third-Person Shooter

Century

An extraction-survival shooter where you scavenge a hostile frontier, haul loot home, and rebuild — the deepest single thing I've built.

In Development · UE 5.8 Solo Developer
  • Grid inventory & equipment — STALKER-style weight/space management, loot, stashing, context actions.
  • Crafting & tech progression — data-driven recipes, furnaces/smelting, a tech tree gated by player level.
  • Vehicles I wrote by hand — a drivable car, a combat tank, and a pilotable mech, no Chaos dependency.
  • Base building & world travel — placeable stations, procedural expeditions, level-to-level travel with saves.
02 / SOULS-LIKE
Dark-Fantasy Souls-Like Action RPG

Call of the Mountains

A brutal, gore-soaked Souls-like — lock-on duels, a Faith economy you lose on death and reclaim where you fell, and "the Forgotten" waiting in ambush.

UE 5.6 Solo Developer
  • Faith economy — Souls-style currency earned from kills, lost on death, recoverable from where you died.
  • Lock-on melee combat — target locking, parries, poise & stagger, finisher kills, weapon combos.
  • Data-driven enemies — "the Forgotten" and variants, incl. molotov-arcing pyromancers, authored from DataTables.
  • Visceral gore tech — real-time dismemberment, blood decals, gore trails, and death effects.
03 / MMORPG
Dark-Fantasy MMORPG

SteelCurtain

A grimdark "iron and ash" RPG with the depth of a classic MMO — classes, talents, threat-driven combat, and a living day/night world.

In Development Solo Developer
  • Class, talent & subclass systems — specializations unlocking at level thresholds, with saved builds.
  • Threat / aggro combat — a full tank-and-spank model: taunts, threat tables, leashing, evade.
  • WoW-style paper-doll UI — live SceneCapture portrait, equipment, a themed grimdark interface layer.
  • A world that changes — replicated day/night, rare blood-moon events that empower the whole map.

How I work
I do a little of everything — working solo means there's no one else to hand a problem to, so I learned to solve all of it. I verify before I call something done: I'd rather have one system that genuinely works than five that only demo well. Every feature here runs in-engine — proof, not promises.
What I'm looking for
A team where demonstrated range matters more than tenure — gameplay programming, technical design, or a hybrid role on an ambitious project. I haven't worked inside a studio yet; I've built the equivalent of one's worth of systems solo. Full-time or contract, remote-friendly.
